exposure: Severity of heart disease (NYHA functional class)
outcome: Prevalence of heart disease in pregnancy
cohort: 53 pregnant women with heart disease out of 9463 pregnancies at a tertiary care teaching hospital in eastern Nepal between March 1st, 2012 and March 31st, 2013
finding: Rheumatic mitral stenosis was the most common heart disease in pregnancy, and exercise intolerance, pulmonary hypertension, and severe mitral stenosis were predictors of maternal or fetal/perinatal mortality.
mod_finding: 44% of women with RHD underwent elective or emergency cesarean section.
